paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : Ablation studies on n-best candidates generations (Beam search and Sampling search) on valid set of WMT15 De-En.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the impact of different n-best candidate generation strategies—beam search and sampling—on the BLEU score as a function of average lagging (AL) in a simultaneous machine translation system, evaluated on the WMT15 De-En validation set. The x-axis, labeled "Average Lagging (AL)", ranges from 2.5 to 12.5, with data points plotted at intervals of 2.5. The y-axis, labeled "BLEU", ranges from 24 to 31, with major gridlines at every unit interval. Three distinct lines represent different configurations: "Inconsistency-CE" (blue circles, dashed line), "Consistency-Bi + sampling" (orange triangles, dashed line), and "Consistency-Bi + beam" (green squares, dashed line). The "Inconsistency-CE" line starts at a BLEU score of approximately 24.0 at AL = 2.5 and rises to about 30.1 at AL = 12.5. The "Consistency-Bi + sampling" line begins at a BLEU score of approximately 27.8 at AL = 2.5 and increases to about 30.8 at AL = 12.5. The "Consistency-Bi + beam" line starts at a BLEU score of approximately 27.5 at AL = 2.5 and increases to about 30.9 at AL = 12.5. All three lines show a general upward trend in BLEU score as average lagging increases, with the "Consistency-Bi + beam" line consistently achieving the highest BLEU scores across the entire range of AL values.
